correctness.rationale: The inequality representation follows from the orthant-wise 0-1 truncated cube with bound 2. At root \(\sigma e_i+\tau e_j\), strict decreasing of all active outer facets gives \(\sigma u_i<0\), \(\tau u_j<0\), and \(2(|u_i|+|u_j|)>\sum_k|u_k|\). Thus one direction covers at most one root per coordinate pair and its heavy coordinate pairs intersect. An intersecting family of edges of a simple graph is a star or triangle, hence cardinality at most \(d-1\) for \(d\ge4\). Summing over all \(2d(d-1)\) vertices gives the fractional lower bound \(2d\). For every center index i, the two vectors with center magnitude d, other magnitudes 1, and sign step at i have precisely its \(d-1\) incident pairs illuminated; the signs from endpoints partition the four roots per coordinate pair exactly once. The 2d directions therefore illuminate every boundary face, proving both upper bounds. The checker independently confirms signed facet tests, exact coverage through dimension 8, and 5440 finite magnitude profiles. None of the finite computations is used for the universal quantification.

originality.rationale: The most relevant previously published same-object result determines a norm-weighted external-point cost of 2d(d-1) and proves a related intersecting-edge restriction. The present statement instead determines ordinary and fractional directional illumination at 2d and gives an explicit signed-direction vertex partition; those do not follow from the previously stated quantitative identity. Foundational 2009 and 2026 fractional results supply general principles, not this evaluated root-polytope family. Prior exact cuboctahedron information concerns dimension three; the novelty-bearing theorem covers all dimensions at least four. All accessible searches and relevant primary inspections were compared at statement and implication level, but unindexed priority remains uncertain.
residual_risks: The closest same-object source already develops the intersecting-coordinate-pair idea, so the proof method is not completely new; priority of the exact signed covering statement requires independent historical review.
An unindexed or unpublished 24-cell or Coxeter-root illumination calculation could provide the same 2d formula.
Database results alone do not prove uniqueness; no independent expert audit has taken place.

value.rationale: The theorem gives exact ordinary and finite fractional illumination for every type-D root polytope in dimensions at least four, explicitly including the exceptional regular four-dimensional 24-cell. Its optimal 2d-direction design is a vertex partition, while a structural intersecting-edge argument certifies that no fractional scheme can improve it. This is an exact natural family classification and a clear contrast to the previously computed quantitative gauge-cost invariant, motivated by contemporary fractional illumination results. The three-dimensional cuboctahedron fact is contextual; the result is not merely a table lookup or isolated low-dimensional computation.
